{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Helen Frances Cullen''' (January 4, 1919 – August 25, 2007){{r|ams}} was an American mathematician specializing in [[topology]]. She worked for many years as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]{{r|amherst}} and was the first female faculty member in the mathematics department at Amherst.{{r|latin}} She was known as the author of the book ''Introduction to General Topology'' (Heath, 1968),{{r|igt}}
as well as for her outspoken [[antisemitism]].{{r|ucu}}

==Education and career==
Cullen was born in [[Dorchester, Massachusetts]], and studied at [[Boston Latin Academy|Girls' Latin School]] and [[Radcliffe College]].{{r|amherst}}
She earned a master's degree at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1944,{{r|regents}}
and completed her Ph.D. at Michigan in 1950. Her dissertation, ''A Set of Parabolic Regular Curve Families Filling the Plane and Certain Related Reimann Surfaces'', was supervised by [[Wilfred Kaplan]].{{r|mgp}} She was a faculty member in the department of mathematics at Amherst from 1949 until her retirement as a [[professor emerita]] in 1992.{{r|amherst}}

==Recognition==
In 1998 the Girls' Latin School – Boston Latin Academy Association listed her as one of their outstanding alumnae.{{r|latin}}
